problem: A particle moves from the origin with an acceleration of $6i\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $-5j\,\text{km/h}.$ Find the position vector of the particle after $3$ hours.

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Position Vector of a Particle Moving With Constant Acceleration
examples.problem: A particle starts moving from the point with position vector $(4\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j})\,\textrm{cm}$ with an acceleration of $(\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j}) \, \textrm{cm/min}^2$ and an initial velocity of $(\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j}) \: \textrm{cm/min}.$ Find the position vector of the particle after $4$ minutes.
examples.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $\mathbf{a},$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{r}_0 + \mathbf{u} t + \dfrac12 \mathbf{a} t^2,
$$

 

where $\mathbf{r}_0$ is the initial position of the particle and $\mathbf{u}$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
\mathbf{r}_0 = 4\mathbf i - \mathbf j , \qquad \mathbf u = \mathbf{i} +\mathbf{j}, \qquad \mathbf a = \mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j}.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t = 4 \, \textrm{min}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(4i-j)+(i+j)(4)+\frac{1}{2}(i+3j)(4)^{2} \\  & =(4i-j)+(4i+4j)+8(i+3j) \\  & =(8i+3j)+(8i+24j) \\  & =(16i+27j)\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: A particle starts moving from the point with position vector $(2i+3j)\,\text{in}$ with a constant velocity of $-j\,\text{in/s}.$ Find the position vector of the particle after $4$ seconds.
feedback.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant velocity $u,$  the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut,
$$

 
where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=2i+3j,\,u=-j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t=4\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & ={r}_{0}+ut \\  & =(2i+3j)+(-j)(4) \\  & =(2i+3j)-4j \\  & =(2i-j)\,\text{in}.\end{aligned}
$$
